# WVU Medicine Jefferson Medical Center breaks ground on campus expansion, advancing access to care in Jefferson County

July 29, 2026

RANSON, W.VA. — WVU Medicine Jefferson Medical Center celebrated the groundbreaking of a major expansion project that will enhance access to healthcare services across Jefferson County and the Eastern Panhandle.

The transformative project represents a $60 million investment in the future of healthcare, bringing expanded outpatient services, advanced clinical capabilities, and a more patient-centered experience to the community.

Image: The groundbreaking at WVU Medicine Jefferson Medical Center July 2026.

The project includes construction of a new three-story ambulatory building that will house medical office space, comprehensive imaging services, and a physical therapy gym.

In addition, renovations are underway inside Jefferson Medical Center to create a new infusion and cancer care suite that will become part of the WVU Cancer Institute, bringing specialized cancer services closer to home for many patients.

# WVU Cancer Institute opens center at WVU Medicine Thomas Memorial Hospital

February 7, 2025

SOUTH CHARLESTON, W.Va – WVU Medicine Thomas Hospitals held a g rand o pening and r ibbon c utting ceremony today (Feb. 7) at th e new WVU Cancer Institute at Thomas Memorial Hospital. T he renovated facility, located at 500 Poplar Street in South Charleston, provides an expanded area for specialized cancer treatment and clinical visits all in one building. 

The new center takes a multidisciplinary approach to medical oncology care, including chemotherapy and other infusion services, a n onsite lab, and a pharmacy planned for later this year, in addition to the radiation oncology services already provided at Thomas. The center include s 17 exam rooms, one procedure room, and 32 infusion bays. Patients will have access to nurse navigation, a telephone triage system for symptom management and prescription refills, tumor boards, and telemedicine appointments.

Image“Since becoming a major hub for WVU Medicine, Thomas Hospitals has expanded services and opened several renovated facilities across its campuses,” Albert L. Wright, Jr., president and CEO of the West Virginia University Health System, said. “The opening of the WVU Cancer Institute at Thomas Memorial Hospital is another example of how we are working to ensure patients in the Kanawha Valley have access to the same quality of care that they can receive at our main campus in Morgantown.” 
 
The new space is four times larger than the previous space, offering a home-like environment with a fireplace, recliners in the infusion center, a healing garden, and hand-picked artwork. The building is easily accessible and has a covered drop-off area at the front doors. Patients may also utilize the free shuttle. 

“A brand new WVU Cancer Institute at Thomas Hospitals brings with it a new era of care for patients,”  Hannah Hazard-Jenkins, M.D., executive chair and director of the WVU Cancer Institute, said. “This isn’t just a bricks-and-mortar investment; it’s an investment in the community and the people of the region who need cancer treatment and can rest assured that the services they need are close to home.” 
 
Physicians are located on the second floor of the building, which was designed to allow them to work out of pods with centralized desks surrounded by exam rooms. The care team works alongside the physicians out of the pods to facilitate efficient communication when patients need extra testing or other resources. 

“Patients are often here for an extended amount of time, so we want them to feel comfortable,” Erin Jackson, director of cancer services at Thomas Hospitals, said. “We are so grateful to provide not only a beautiful space, but a more convenient facility for our patients. We are now able to accommodate more patients with added chairs and c annot wait to continue to expand our services.” 

The WVU Cancer Institute at Thomas Memorial Hospital is a full service, regional treatment center, offering a compassionate and supportive atmosphere, along with advanced medical cancer treatment. Thomas Hospitals’ clinicians treat virtually every type of cancer, including breast, lung, colorectal, prostate, head and neck, brain, gynecologic, skin, and hematological disorders. 

“At Thomas Hospitals, we are committed to providing residents of southern West Virginia and surrounding areas with high-quality oncology care without having to travel far from home,” Greg Rosencrance, M.D., president and CEO of Thomas Hospitals, said. “Our caregivers and patients have shared positive feedback regarding the new space, and our talented and experienced team is pleased to offer individualized, compassionate care in a state-of-the-art WVU Cancer Institute facility.” 

Patients wishing to schedule medical oncology and infusion appointments at Thomas Hospitals can call 304-766-4350.

For more information on the WVU Cancer Institute, visit WVUMedicine.org/Cancer. For more information on WVU Medicine Thomas Hospitals, visit ThomasHospitals.org.

# Princeton Community Hospital kicks off construction of comprehensive cancer center

## Project is the largest cancer care investment ever in the region

August 21, 2025

PRINCETON, W.Va. – WVU Medicine Princeton Community Hospital (PCH) today hosted a ceremony to mark the start of construction on a two-story, 45,500-square-foot comprehensive cancer center that will bring advanced cancer care closer to home for patients across Southern West Virginia and Southwest Virginia.

The over-$35 million project represents the largest investment in cancer services ever made in the region and underscores WVU Medicine’s commitment to improving access to world-class care in communities in every part of the state. 

“Through WVU Medicine Princeton Community Hospital, West Virginia University is investing in the health of people in communities across southern West Virginia, ensuring that those who need cancer treatment can access care close to home from world-class providers,” said Michael T.   * Convenient patient drop-off and accessible parking create a low-stress arrival, while expanded staff parking supports the growing care team.
  * A dedicated ambulance drop-off for emergent cases ensures rapid access when needed.

Comprehensive Cancer Care

The center will integrate services in one location for patient convenience and continuity of care:

  * A direct connection to the existing oncology clinic for seamless coordination of care.
  * A light-filled infusion center with glass walls offering natural views and social interaction opportunities during treatment.
  * Decentralized nurse stations throughout the facility to strengthen staff-patient connection.
  * A full-service pharmacy to support comprehensive treatment plans.

A New Era of Cancer Care

When completed in late 2027, the cancer center will house the latest, most-advanced technologies including a Varian Halcyon linear accelerator for radiation therapy and treatments, and a CT scanner that enhances diagnostic precision to aid in treatment planning.

# WVU Medicine Princeton Community Hospital begins cancer center project with demolition

## WVU Medicine Princeton Community Hospital marked the start of its Comprehensive Cancer Center project with demolition of the former laundry facility, paving the way for expanded cancer care in the region.

  * From Staff Reports
  * Apr 7, 2026

WVU Medicine Princeton Community Hospital has begun the next phase of its Comprehensive Cancer Center project with demolition of its former laundry facility in Princeton.

PRINCETON, W.Va. — WVU Medicine Princeton Community Hospital has officially launched the next phase of its Comprehensive Cancer Center project with the demolition of its former laundry facility.

Hospital leaders, staff and community partners gathered to mark the milestone, recognizing the facility’s history while looking ahead to expanded cancer care services for the region.

“This moment represents both reflection and transformation,” said Karen Bowling, MSN, RN, president and CEO of PCH. “For decades, this facility supported patient care in important ways. Today, we honor that legacy as we begin building something new—a cancer center that will change the future of care for our region.”

Constructed in the 1990s, the laundry facility once handled thousands of pounds of linens per hour through an automated system and played a key role in daily hospital operations. During the ceremony, Bowling acknowledged former department leaders and staff, including Marvin McClanahan and Wilma Wade, for their contributions.

The demolition signals the start of construction on a new $35 million comprehensive cancer center. The planned 45,500-square-foot facility will bring multiple cancer care services under one roof.

Once completed, the center will offer medical oncology, infusion therapy, advanced imaging and radiation therapy. Hospital officials said the facility will incorporate modern technology aimed at improving early detection, diagnosis and targeted treatment.

“This is about more than a building,” Bowling said. “It’s about creating a place of hope—where patients can receive life-saving care close to home, and where the future of cancer care in our region begins.”

Construction is expected to be completed in 2027, expanding access to specialized care for patients across southern West Virginia and neighboring areas.
